dedupe_keys.name: openpytea process plant techno economic assessment

description: OpenPyTEA is a Python toolkit developed at TU Delft for economic assessment of chemical and energy process plants. It combines equipment cost correlations, capital and operating expenditure calculations, cash-flow analysis, sensitivity tests and Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation. Users supply equipment sizes, process-simulation results, prices and financial assumptions. Outputs include cost breakdowns, net present value, payback time and levelized product costs. Geography, currency assumptions and project lifetime are user-defined; the package is not a fixed national cost dataset. The public repository supplies Python modules, JSON workflows, documentation and worked notebooks. Code is free under MIT. These tools support comparisons of hydrogen, geothermal and other process-infrastructure designs. A limitation is that economic results depend on cost correlations, location factors and external engineering inputs; the package does not solve process mass and energy balances itself. Its optional graphical interface remains under development. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. This review checked documentation without installing software or running economic analyses.
